vote: The should-it-exist tree was applied in order and correctly (existing-artifact check first, recurring linear single-agent recipe -> skill) and the type-depth rule was honored by dispatching skill-author, so the front half of the skill worked as written. But the line logs outcome success with no evidence for the contract's acceptance gate: nothing says evals/run.sh was executed, that the 6 non-holdout cases passed, or that the holdout held - authoring a harness is not the same as 'a draft goes live only when every non-holdout case passes.' The excerpt also never mentions the new artifact's votes/votes.jsonl or its terminal '## logging' section, both explicit not-done conditions in the contract, and it does not say templates/eval-harness.md was copied versus a bespoke harness written. Three artifact gaps this use exposes: (1) the contract lists deliverables but gives the logger nothing to attest, so success lines can silently skip the go-live gate - add a required gate field to the logging format (cases passed X/Y, holdout held) so 'success' means gate-passed, not author-finished; (2) the exam fence only binds the GEPA mutation-proposer, yet here one authoring pass wrote both the recipe and its evals/rubric - state explicitly whether initial authoring needs the same fence or why it does not; (3) seeding logs from a pre-skill run is sensible GEPA bootstrapping but nothing in the skill sanctions or formats retroactive lines, and that seeded line arguably should have triggered a blind judge vote for the new create-pr artifact per the judge protocol. The repeated failure this use hints at: outcome success recorded at author-time rather than at gate-time, which will inflate the reflective dataset with unverified wins.
